visual.general_description: Eleven-panel figure with one chest radiograph (A) and ten axial chest CT images (B to K) arranged in two rows of five under the radiograph.
visual.detailed_description: Panel A is a grayscale frontal chest radiograph at the upper left. Below it, the upper row has five axial lung-window CT images (B, D, F, H, J) at the level of the main bronchi, and the lower row has five axial images through the lung bases (C, E, G, I, K); four of the lower images are doubled by a thin vertical black line into left and right halves. Black arrows appear in D, H, C, E and I and arrowheads in G and K. No numeric values, dates or patient text are visible.

panels.detailed_description: Grayscale frontal chest radiograph showing both lungs, the mediastinal and cardiac silhouette and upper abdomen; the panel letter A is printed at the upper left. No arrows, measurements or other text are visible.

Images from chest radiography and high-resolution computed tomography. Chest X-ray showing ground-glass attenuation (GGA) and volume loss, predominantly in the bilateral lower lung field (A). Chest high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) showing GGA with traction bronchiectasis (black arrows), predominantly in the bilateral lower lung lobes (B,C). Enlargement of the GGA with traction bronchiectasis (black arrows) in the bilateral lungs are observed (D,E). Reduced GGA and worsening traction bronchiectasis (arrow heads) are demonstrated (F,G). Greater enlargement of the GGA with traction bronchiectasis (black arrows) are exhibited (H,I). Reduced bilateral GGA (J,K).
